name: Semma
description: Chef Vijay Kumar's personal tribute to Tamil Nadu's cuisine — fiery, coconut-rich Southern Indian cooking that transformed how New York thinks about Indian food.

name: Atomix
description: Junghyun and Ellia Park's subterranean Korean tasting menu, where each course arrives with a handwritten card and punchy, modern technique.

name: Le Bernardin
description: Eric Ripert's four-star seafood institution where pristine fish and precise French technique have earned an unbroken run at the top of New York dining for 30 years.

name: Kabawa
description: Paul Carmichael's joyful Caribbean kitchen in the former Momofuku Ko space, serving a three-course prix fixe of vibrant Barbadian-rooted dishes with tie-dyed warmth.

name: Ha's Snack Bar
description: Anthony Ha and Sadie Mae Burns-Ha's permanent home for their celebrated pop-up, blending Vietnamese and French flavors with seasonal precision and a great natural wine list.

name: King
description: Clare de Boer's intimate South Village room celebrated for rustic, vegetable-forward Mediterranean cooking with whole-roasted meats and impeccable sourcing.

name: Penny
description: A new East Village spot marrying French technique with pristine seafood in a relaxed setting.

name: Sushi Sho
description: A reverent omakase counter from a Tokyo master, where each bite-sized piece of sushi is seasoned and served at the precise moment of perfection.

name: Szechuan Mountain House
address: 23 St. Marks Place, New York, NY 10003
description: The East Village's most electrifying Szechuan table — numbing peppercorns, chili oil, and bold umami in a casual, welcoming room.

name: Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi
address: 10 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023
description: Kwame Onwuachi's love letter to the African diaspora — jerk chicken, goat roti, and Creole flavors served at Lincoln Center with serious style.

name: 188 Bakery Cuchifritos
description: A beloved Bronx counter known for its cuchifritos — fried pork specialties and Puerto Rican pastries that are the real deal.

name: A&A Bake and Doubles
description: Brooklyn's best doubles — the beloved Trinidadian street food sandwich of fried bara bread with curried chickpeas, tamarind, and pepper sauce.

name: AbuQir Seafood
description: An Egyptian seafood institution in Astoria where whole fish is fried or grilled to order and the atmosphere is pure neighborhood warmth.

name: Aska
description: Fredrik Berselius's Scandinavian tasting menu in Williamsburg — moody, foraged, and ethereally precise, channeling the Nordic wilderness through Brooklyn.

name: Atoboy
description: The more accessible sibling of Atomix — choose-your-own Korean banchan-style sharing plates in a warm, approachable setting.

name: Barbuto
description: Jonathan Waxman's Italian-inflected New American landmark, famous for its roast chicken and the breezy garage-door dining room.

name: Barney Greengrass
description: The century-old 'Sturgeon King' of the Upper West Side — the city's gold standard for smoked fish, cream cheese, and an unimprovable bagel.

name: Birria-Landia
description: The Queens truck-turned-storefront that put birria tacos on the map — deeply spiced consommé, tender beef, and perfectly crispy-dipped tortillas.

name: Borgo
description: A new Midtown Italian spot earning praise for its regional Italian cooking and well-edited wine list.

name: Bridges
description: A new American-French kitchen in Chinatown drawing on the neighborhood's energy for an inventive, produce-driven menu.

name: Bungalow
description: A new East Village Indian restaurant bringing regional Indian cooking with modern sensibility to a neighborhood already rich with South Asian food.

name: Cafe Kestrel
description: A destination Red Hook restaurant with a European-leaning menu that rewards the trip from Manhattan.

name: Cafe Mado
description: A neighborhood gem in Prospect Heights serving thoughtful New American food with French inflections in a warm, intimate setting.

name: Carnitas Ramirez
description: A tiny East Village counter devoted to carnitas — slow-cooked pork done right, served in tacos and tortas at very reasonable prices.

name: Casa Mono and Bar Jamón
description: Mario Batali's Spanish tapas bar (now under new leadership) near Gramercy Park — one of NYC's best spots for Iberian small plates and jamón.

name: Cervo's
description: A sun-drenched Portuguese and Spanish wine bar on Canal Street, beloved for its tinned fish, fresh seafood, and natural wine selection.

name: Chambers
description: A smart TriBeCa American restaurant earning attention for its precise, ingredient-driven cooking.

name: Chez Ma Tante
description: A beloved Greenpoint neighborhood restaurant with a European-leaning menu, famous for its Dutch baby pancake brunch and relaxed dinner service.

name: Cho Dang Gol
description: A Koreatown institution specializing in house-made tofu — soft, silken, and used in every form across a menu of classic Korean comfort food.

name: Chongqing Lao Zao
description: Flushing's most exciting Chongqing restaurant, bringing the fiery, numbing street food of Sichuan's mountain city to Queens.

name: Çka Ka Qëllu
description: The Bronx's Arthur Avenue gets a taste of the Balkans at this Albanian restaurant serving hearty, meat-forward dishes in a welcoming family environment.

name: Claud
description: A French-inflected East Village newcomer with a wine-bar sensibility — the kind of effortless cooking that makes everything look easy.

name: Cocina Consuelo
description: A Harlem Mexican kitchen serving the homestyle cooking of Oaxaca and Puebla with heart and generosity.

name: Court Street Grocers
description: Brooklyn's most beloved sandwich shop — a grocery and deli combining exceptional ingredients with thoughtful, creative sandwich-making.

name: Crown Shy
description: James Kent's sophisticated Financial District restaurant in a landmark Art Deco tower, with ambitious American cooking and a serious bar program.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel Boulud's crown jewel — a palatial Upper East Side French restaurant where classical technique and seasonal luxury define one of the city's great fine dining experiences.

name: Dera
description: A Jackson Heights restaurant serving the authentic subcontinental cooking of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and India to a diverse neighborhood clientele.

name: Dhamaka
description: Chintan Pandya's temple to the rustic cooking of rural India — offal curries, whole roasted lamb, and the kind of bold flavors rarely seen in NYC.

name: Don Peppe
address: 135-58 Lefferts Boulevard, South Ozone Park, NY 11420
description: A no-frills Queens Italian-American institution in business for over 50 years — cash only, no menu, and whatever they feel like cooking that day.

name: Ewe's Delicious Treats
description: A Nigerian-owned Brooklyn bakery and snack shop serving West African sweets, savories, and a taste of home for the local community.

name: Eyval
description: An Iranian restaurant in Bushwick bringing the aromatic, herb-rich cooking of Persia to New York with warmth and contemporary sensibility.

name: The Four Horsemen
description: James Murphy's (of LCD Soundsystem) celebrated natural wine bar in Williamsburg, pairing an exceptional bottle list with smart, ingredient-driven small plates.

name: Four Twenty Five
description: Le Bernardin's Eric Ripert opens a second Midtown chapter — a polished American restaurant in a stunning Norman Foster tower on Park Avenue.

name: Frenchette
description: Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson's influential TriBeCa bistro — a modern Paris brasserie that helped launch NYC's natural wine and casual French fine-dining moment.

name: Gage & Tollner
description: A stunning Victorian restaurant resurrected in Downtown Brooklyn, serving refined American seafood in the city's most beautiful dining room.

name: Golden Diner
description: Sam Yoo's celebrated Chinatown diner blending classic American diner comfort with East Asian flavors — the egg sandwich is legendary.

name: Gramercy Tavern
description: Danny Meyer's flagship and one of New York's most beloved restaurants — consistently excellent New American cooking in a warm, flowers-and-wood room.

name: Great N.Y. Noodletown
description: A Chinatown institution open until 4am, renowned for its roast meats, soft-shell crab in season, and no-frills Hong Kong-style noodles.

name: The Grill
description: The restored Four Seasons space reimagined as a power-lunch institution with tableside preparations, perfectly aged steaks, and 1960s Mad Men glamour.

name: Hainan Chicken House
description: A Sunset Park spot devoted to Hainanese chicken rice — silky poached chicken, fragrant rice cooked in chicken fat, and three essential dipping sauces.

name: Hamburger America
description: George Motz's burger shrine opened as a brick-and-mortar after decades as a documentary and pop-up — regional American burgers done with obsessive fidelity.

name: Hellbender
description: A Ridgewood Mexican spot earning serious attention for its nuanced, regional Mexican cooking far from the standard taco shop playbook.

name: Ho Foods
description: A tiny East Village noodle shop serving Taiwanese beef noodle soup with a deeply spiced, slow-cooked broth that's become one of the city's cult bowls.

name: Houseman
description: Ned Baldwin's cozy Hudson Square restaurant that emphasizes offal, whole-animal cooking, and the pleasures of unfashionable cuts done brilliantly.

name: Jean-Georges
address: 1 Central Park West, New York, NY 10023
description: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's flagship in the Trump International Hotel — one of NYC's last great four-star French restaurants, with iconic dishes spanning 30+ years.

name: Jeju Noodle Bar
description: A West Village spot devoted to ramyun and Korean noodles with thoughtful depth — the pork broth is rich and meticulously made.

name: Jungsik
description: Jungsik Yim's TriBeCa Korean fine dining — seasonal ingredients and French technique applied to Korean flavor principles at the highest level.

name: Keens
description: A Manhattan institution since 1885 — the legendary mutton chop and clay pipes hanging from the ceiling make Keens one of the most atmospheric rooms in the city.

name: Kisa
address: Lower East Side, New York, NY 10002
description: A Korean restaurant on the Lower East Side praised for its precise, well-sourced Korean cooking that earns comparison to the best in Koreatown.

name: Koloman
description: A Viennese cafe and restaurant in the Ace Hotel bringing the elegance of Central European coffee culture and cuisine to NoMad.

name: Kono
description: An intimate Japanese omakase counter in Chinatown earning acclaim for its austere, meditative approach to sushi and kaiseki preparation.

name: Kopitiam
description: NYC's best Malaysian coffee shop — Kyo Pang's Chinatown spot serves the hawker-stall classics of Kuala Lumpur in a cheerful, tile-lined room.

name: Laghman Express
description: A Uyghur restaurant in Bensonhurst serving hand-pulled laghman noodles and the bold, cumin-spiced cooking of Central Asia.

name: Lakruwana
description: A Sri Lankan restaurant on Staten Island serving the aromatic, coconut-rich cooking of the island — one of the few places in NYC for this underrepresented cuisine.

name: Le Coucou
description: Daniel Rose's soaringly beautiful SoHo French restaurant — one of the most romantic dining rooms in New York, with classical technique and a perfectly curated cheese cart.

name: Le Veau d'Or
description: A revived Upper East Side French classic — the tiny bistro that's been feeding the neighborhood for decades, now back at its best.

name: Levant
description: A new Astoria restaurant bringing the vibrant flavors of the Levant — mezze, grilled meats, and spiced vegetables — to a Queens neighborhood.

name: Lilia
description: Missy Robbins's brilliant Williamsburg pasta shrine — the mafaldini with pink peppercorns is one of the city's greatest dishes.

name: Little Myanmar
description: NYC's leading Burmese restaurant, serving the distinctive fermented tea leaf salads and aromatic curries of Myanmar to an appreciative East Village crowd.

name: Lola's
description: A new NoMad spot fusing Asian and Southern American flavors in an unexpected and exciting way.

name: Lucia Pizza of Avenue X
description: A Sheepshead Bay Neapolitan pizza destination drawing pilgrims to Brooklyn's southern tip for impeccably charred, airy pies.

name: Mắm
address: Lower East Side, New York, NY 10002
description: A Vietnamese restaurant on the Lower East Side showcasing the fermented, funky, and complex flavors of Hanoi and the north.

name: Okdongsik
description: A new Koreatown arrival elevating Korean comfort food with careful sourcing and technique.

name: Okiboru House of Tsukemen
address: Lower East Side, New York, NY 10002
description: NYC's dedicated tsukemen (dipping ramen) shop, where thick noodles are dipped in a rich, concentrated broth — a ramen format rarely seen outside Japan.

name: Old Sport
description: A Forest Hills halal Chinese restaurant bringing the bold flavors of northwestern China — cumin lamb, hand-pulled noodles — to a Queens neighborhood.

name: Raf's
address: 2 Great Jones Street, New York, NY 10012
description: A romantic French-Italian restaurant in NoHo with candlelit booths, excellent pasta, and the feel of a private Parisian supper club.

name: Raku
description: A Japanese restaurant specializing in udon and various small plates, with a cozy East Village following for its careful, understated cooking.

name: Randazzo's Clam Bar
description: A beloved Sheepshead Bay landmark on the water, serving Italian-American seafood classics in a family atmosphere that feels frozen in the best possible way.

name: S & P Lunch
description: A beloved no-frills Flatiron lunch counter serving old-school deli sandwiches and soups to generations of New Yorkers since the 1950s.

name: Sailor
description: A Fort Greene restaurant evoking the cooking of the British Isles and Mediterranean with warm hospitality and natural wine.

name: Salty Lunch Lady's Little Luncheonette
description: A Ridgewood sandwich shop earning a cult following for its creative, well-constructed sandwiches in an unpretentious neighborhood setting.

name: Shaw-naé's House
description: A Staten Island soul food destination where Shaw-naé's home cooking tradition — fried chicken, collard greens, mac and cheese — draws diners from across the city.

name: Shukette
description: A Chelsea Middle Eastern wine bar from the Shuka team, combining Israeli-inspired mezze, natural wine, and a lively, intimate vibe.

name: Sofreh
description: Nasim Alikhani's elegant Persian restaurant in Prospect Heights — the finest Iranian cooking in New York, with the warmth of a family table.

name: Superiority Burger
description: Brooks Headley's legendary vegetarian burger shop — the impossible-to-categorize East Village spot where the veggie burger is legitimately the best burger in the city.

name: Sushi Noz
description: An intimate Upper East Side omakase counter where chef Nozomu Abe uses aged fish and slow fermentation to create sushi unlike anything else in New York.

name: Sushi Ouji
description: A SoHo omakase that earns its place at the top of NYC's competitive sushi scene with precision, personality, and exceptional sourcing.

name: Taiwanese Gourmet
description: A Queens Taiwanese restaurant beloved for its home-style cooking — three-cup chicken, oyster vermicelli, and the kind of food you'd find at a family table in Taipei.

name: Temple Canteen
description: A Flushing Indian spot serving the vegetarian cooking associated with temple kitchens — pure, aromatic, and deeply satisfying.

name: Thai Diner
description: Ann Redding and Matt Danzer's Thai diner on Mott Street — the creative successors to Uncle Boons, blending American diner comfort with bold Thai flavor.

name: Third Falcon
description: A Fort Greene restaurant marrying French bistro precision with American hospitality in a warmly lit neighborhood room.

name: Torrisi
description: Rich Torrisi's flagship return — an Italian-American restaurant that treats the canon with deep respect and brilliant technique in a buzzy NoLIta room.

name: Trinciti Roti Shop
description: A Queens Trinidadian roti shop beloved by the South Asian Caribbean community — buss-up-shut, doubles, and curried meats wrapped in flaky paratha.

name: Txikito
description: Alex Raij's Chelsea Basque restaurant — pintxos, salt cod, and cider in a warm, idiosyncratic room that feels transported from San Sebastián.

name: Una Pizza Napoletana
description: Anthony Mangieri's legendary Neapolitan pizza shop — only a handful of pies served, only on certain days, but they may be the finest pizza in New York.

name: Via Carota
description: Jody Williams and Rita Sodi's beloved West Village Italian trattoria — the insalata verde is perfect, the pasta is better, and the room is always packed.

name: Village Café
description: A Brooklyn Azerbaijani restaurant serving the hearty, aromatic cooking of the South Caucasus — dolma, kebabs, and fragrant rice dishes.

name: White Bear
description: A tiny Flushing counter famous for wontons — spicy, hand-folded, and served in a chile oil so good people order extra just to drink it.

name: Yoon Haeundae Galbi
description: A Koreatown Korean BBQ specialist focused on Haeundae-style galbi — premium short ribs marinated and grilled tableside in an upscale but lively room.

name: Zaab Zaab
description: Queens' essential Isaan Thai restaurant — funky, fermented, fiercely spiced northeastern Thai cooking from a family kitchen with no interest in softening anything.
